lane_constraints: All modules are included into basm.c, not separate module objects. The Bear product uses blibc string.h macro mapping memcmp to bear_memcmp; inspect selected object relocations and final linkage before claiming reachability.
Symbol lookup checks hash and length before comparing nl bytes. Names are public; an equality-only helper may replace this use, not the public lexicographic memcmp contract.
Preserve unsigned byte ordering in bear_memcmp. Secret equality belongs to bear_ct_memcmp, never the early-exit name lookup.

lane_constraints: sha256_ni.h enables SHA256NI_X86 only for __x86_64__ and not __bear__. The Bear product compiles software compression even on a SHA-capable host.
Host test_sha or a host CC basm may use intrinsics; neither demonstrates accelerated SHA in the Bear-built product.
Attestation hashes tool, source and object through basm_sha_file. sign.c hashes proof bodies with the separate sgn_ namespace. Unsigned workload proofs do not exercise signing.
Rel8 escrow may select bear_sha256_* under BEAR_TIME_H rather than this header's implementation; do not conflate escrow with basm_sha_file.
Future SHA-NI requires SHA plus SSSE3/SSE4.1 and permitted OS/domain state; retain software, tails, padding and streaming equivalence. No host execution of ring0 candidates.
consumers.workload_gap: Fixed unsigned attestation assembly is only groundwork. Separate hash-kernel and consumer timings, selected static call sites and signing workloads remain unmeasured.
